text:
jing: Heads up — brought up a new model build (Zephyr-XL-v0.9 from partner). Quick smoke: generation looks fine FP32 but int8/4 quantized runs show consistent hallucination on long context and token repetition after ~512 tokens.

maya: can you paste a minimal repro and perf numbers?

jing: perf: fp32 baseline 18 tok/s on A6000, int8 ~55 tok/s but quality drops. Repro: simple prompt + long context file (attached). Also notice the KV cache seems to fall out of sync during generation.

liam: did you check rotary params / head ordering? sounds like a head-dim/headwise mismatch.

jing: yeah suspicious — exported with onnx-converter that sets head_dim=64, but model originally exported with head_dim=32 and head count remapped. We see odd phase wrap signs in the logits.

sara: probable sources: (1) rotary scale/half-angle mismatch (2) tokenizer vocab mapping shift (3) kv cache token id offset when remapping vocab. Any logs from token ids?

jing: quick diff of token ids for same string across tokenizers:
```
# id mapping snippet
orig_tok.encode("The quick brown fox") -> [12, 45, 391, 78]
new_tok.encode("The quick brown fox")  -> [12, 45, 392, 78]  # single-token drift at 'brown'
```
small off-by-one in middle of tokenmap.

maya: that explains content drift leading to repetition later. If kvcache uses ids from new tokenizer but rotary/weights built for original ids, alignment breaks.

liam: experiments to run: A) remap tokenizer to original token ids before quant conversion, B) force-headwise-rotary toggle during runtime (swap head order), C) run a kvcache-offset patch that subtracts observed delta for early tokens.

jing: I'll run A and C today. For B we need a small runtime flag — @deploy-bot can you create a short-lived branch with headwise-rotary toggle?

deploy-bot: branch created: feature/rotary-toggle-2249999999, snapshot id s-20240321-312. :white_check_mark:

sara: for reproducibility also upload the diff embedding matrices and a small golden output (fp32) to the eval bucket. I'll run automated evals.

jing: done, uploaded to s3://rwd-inference-evals/zephyr-xl/v0.9/fp32_golden.json

maya: allocation note — quantized runs are faster but we must track quality per-token: add a sliding-window perplexity check. I can add it to the eval harness.

liam: ping when branch is ready, I'll try runtime swap and a head-dim reorder shim. If that improves alignment we can add convert-time remap.

jing: quick temp patch I used to test kv offset:
```
# tiny shim
def apply_kv_offset(kv, token_ids, offset):
    token_ids = [t - offset for t in token_ids]
    return kv_reindex(kv, token_ids)
```
worked for short runs (no repetition for another 2k tokens) but needs robust mapping table.

sara: good sign. Can you produce a small ablation table: fp32 vs int8 vs int4 with/without remap/kvfix/rotary-toggle? Put in the report.

jing: on it. Initial numbers:
- fp32 baseline: perplexity on eval set 12.4
- int8 w/o fixes: 29.7
- int8 + kv-offset: 15.9
- int8 + tokenizer-remap: 13.1

maya: that suggests most of the degradation was vocab/kvcache misalignment, rotary/head ordering second-order. Great.

liam: action items: 1) maya add sliding perplexity to eval harness (assigned) 2) jing produce conversion script to remap token ids and bake into quant conversion (assigned) 3) sara run full eval matrix and file regression ticket if any remaining gaps (assigned).

jing: I'll open PR for conversion script and add testcases. Will include mapping verifier and token-roundtrip checks.

deploy-bot: PR created: rwd/zephyr-converters#512 (refs feature/rotary-toggle-2249999999)

maya: nice. also add a quick smoke that runs 1k token generation with cached tokens to catch late drift.

sara: if all good we can onboard Zephyr-XL to the model catalog as "verified-rotary-vocab-remap" and add recommended quant profile.

liam: FYI — let's also add a note to model onboarding doc about checking token id stability when ingesting external checkpoints. This keeps recurring problems down.

jing: agreed. I'll draft a short checklist and attach to the PR.

maya: thanks team — looks like a good plan. :thumbsup:

jing: closing thread after PR lands, will update here.
